REGISTRATION

KAÇKAR 100K

A 100K that feels like a 100M.

The Kaçkar Mountains will test not only your legs but your spirit. With 82 km of distance and 5,600 m of elevation gain, this course demands everything - endurance, focus, and respect for the mountains.

You’ll climb high ridgelines, cross remote valleys, and pass through 12 mountain villages, each revealing a different side of Kaçkar’s wild heart. Between emerald forests, roaring rivers, and endless ascents above the clouds, the line between challenge and survival begins to blur.

Those who stand at the start of Kaçkar 100K should know: this is not a typical 100K. It feels far longer, far harder, a true mountain ultra that pushes even experienced trail runners to their limits.

If you are questioning whether you’re ready, maybe Kaçkar 50K is where your Kaçkar journey should begin.

LET'S DISCOVER KAÇKAR 100K

Hazindak

A wild section of primary forest — steep, narrow, raw, and full of river crossings. Fallen trees, deep moss, and a true “into the wild” feeling.

Altitude: 1932 m

Stage Distance: 8.5 km Stage Ascent: 1044 m Stage Descent: 453 m

Total Distance: 8.5 km Total Ascent: 1044 m Total Descent: 453 m

See more

Samistal

A remote stone-house plateau overlooking endless ridgelines. Historic shepherd trails and grassy slopes guide runners toward the high pass.

See more

Yukarı Kavrun

A wide mountain basin marking the entrance toward Mezovit. Open, airy, and framed by the Kaçkar giants — a deep breath before the serious climbs begin.

See more

Mezovit/Öküzyatağı

A remote alpine meadow known as the “bed of bulls,” surrounded by raw high mountains. Kaçkar Glacier appears on the right as runners follow the river upward into isolation.

See more

Mezovit Pass

A demanding rocky scramble to 3200m — thin air, sharp peaks, and mesmerizing views of lakes and Kaçkar’s dramatic north face.

See more

Lakes Area

Two large alpine lakes sitting between Serdal and Ceymakcur passes. Technical, rocky, and endlessly beautiful — a true high-mountain environment.

See more

Yukarı Çeymakçur

Ancient rock-laid paths run along the river, leading once again into a steep, technical climb toward Palakcur.

See more

Palakçur

A tiny mountain village facing the great peak of Sele — peaceful but followed by a steep grassy climb that wakes up the legs.

See more

Palakçur Pass/Avusor Lake

A long traverse at 2700m where the valley opens wide. Meadows, river crossings, and a final steep push reveal the bright turquoise Avusor Lake — a true gem of the Kaçkars.

See more

Avusor/Life Base

A lively mountain settlement backed by towering peaks. Runners refuel here before tackling the high passes beyond.

See more

Dadala Pansion

A vast alpine plateau with sweeping views of Altınparmak Mountain. The route crosses the Dadala Pass at nearly 2900m before plunging into a wide, runnable valley.

See more

Koçdüzü

Technical but runable trail down from Dadala Pansion towards the pass to Koçdüzü. Nice views of the Altiparmak in the back. Well runable but technical downhill to the village of Koçdüzü near the lake.

See more

Huser

High above the clouds, this balcony ridge blends runnable terrain with jaw-dropping panoramas and the iconic giant swings floating over the valleys.

See more

Huser Trail

A steep descent through deep, untouched woods that hits you fast — raw, quiet, and beautifully wild.

See more

Ayder

A lively mountain village surrounded by steam, springs, and forested slopes — the perfect mix of buzz and wilderness to start and finish your Kaçkar journey.

See more

EQUIPMENT / COURSE 100K
  Clothing and Footwear:
1 Closed trail running shoes with tread outsole X
2 Running backpack (or for 20K - running belt) with mandatory equipment X
3 Fully functioning headlamp and external batteries 2
4 Cap, bandana or buff X
5 Waterproof jacket with hood X
6 Warm second layer (fleece, down or insulation jacket) X
7 Long-legged trousers or race leggings or a combination of leggings and long socks to cover the legs completely X
8 Sunglasses X
9 Trail Running Crampons/Snowchains X
10 Warm and water-proof gloves *regular cotton gloves + a surgery glove over it to make it waterproof X
  Equipment:
11 Health report or athlete licence X
12 ID - Passport / ID card X
13 GPS Tracker (Included in the registration fee) X
14 Smartphone with international roaming and LiveTrail app downloaded (switched on and airplane mode turned off) X
15 Reusable cup (150 ml minimum) for drink X
16 Reusable plate or bowl and cutlery (Bring Your Own Utensils - BYOU) X
17 Capacity to fluids 1.5L
  Emergency:
18 Survival blanket (min 1.4m x 2m) X
19 Whistle X
20 Elastic Tape and Bandage (min 100x6cm) X
21 Food reserve (800 kcal) X

X: Mandatory equipment (must be carried at all times
O: Non-mandatory equipment

Privacy Preference Center

When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. Click on the different category headings to find out more and change our default settings. However, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience of the site and the services we are able to offer.

Manage Consent Preferences

Strictly Necessary Cookies

Always Active

These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

Functional Cookies

These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Performance Cookies

These cookies allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. All information these cookies collect is aggregated and therefore anonymous. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site, and will not be able to monitor its performance.

Targeting Cookies

These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
